title: The memory palace was the first page table
lede: Virtual memory outside the computer: a design two thousand years old, a mechanism in the brain, and the traffic that runs both ways.
description: A computer with virtual memory lets a program use more memory than the machine has. The same arrangement is found outside computers: whole in warehouses, in part in the brain, and designed two thousand years ago in the memory palace.

meta.Part of: Simonides, a research project on virtual memory outside the computer

excerpt: What computers call virtual memory is a bundle of five things. Outside the computer, the whole bundle is found in warehouses; the index and the fault are found in the brain; and the oldest designed version is Roman.
og_alt: A painted limestone wall of nine arched niches behind a sunlit stone ledge, bronze lamps hanging in three of them, a folded wax tablet and stylus in one, and an ultramarine silk spilling from it down onto the ledge; an olive tree, hills and a golden sea beyond.
